status: proposed; awaiting advisor selection; no round2 execution yet
title: Generalized thermal amplitude damping with signed heat ledger
goal: Expose omitted reservoir input and distinguish stored energy from extractable work while retaining exact zero-temperature compatibility.
outputScope: Only panel/energy/ standalone exploratory implementation and independent test; integration is advisor-owned.

variables.nu: bath stationary excited population in [0,1]; [0,1/2] ordinary nonnegative-temperature bath, >1/2 inverted resource

model.closure: E_out-E_in-Q=0 for this fixed-H channel model
model.ergotropy: E_out minus gap times smallest eigenvalue of rho_out

independentOracle: Direct matrix action of four generalized-amplitude-damping Kraus operators, followed by a separate dephasing channel; eigenvalues from independent Hermitian eigensolver.
acceptance: Direct Kraus action and scalar prediction agree over a frozen finite grid, including boundary cases.
Trace one and nonnegative spectrum within stated floating-point tolerance.
gamma=0 identity before optional dephasing; gamma=1 thermal population and zero coherence; nu=0 matches existing quantum.mjs.
Signed heat closure holds, including heating and cooling.
Every diagonal thermal fixed point nu<=1/2 has zero ergotropy even when energy is positive.
For 0<nu<1/2, entropy production DeltaS - log((1-nu)/nu)*Q/gap is nonnegative within tolerance.
All wrong-model controls below fail the corresponding conservation/passivity criterion with nonzero margins.

wrongModelControls.error: Set heat input to zero and call output energy new work.
Use W=E for passive thermal diagonal state.
Retain old environment loss gamma*gap*p after allowing bath excitation.

exclusions: No proof of OpenAI capacity/additivity theorem.
Finite numerical sampling is not a proof over a continuous parameter domain.
allowedAnalyticLemma: For the displayed channel and fixed H, heat into the battery equals gap*gamma*(nu-p); positive-temperature diagonal fixed points are passive. Both are elementary identities, not novel theorem discoveries.
